rules.statement: Don't report a documentation evidence or proof-link entry for naming a file or line range that has since moved, when the entry pins a commit at which that file and range were correct and the pinned commit stays reachable.
rules.why: The evidence check and the site links read each range at the pinned commit, so the entries are correct; pointing them at today's files without moving the pin would break the check.
rules.check: Before reporting a stale file/line reference in an evidence file, look for a pinned commit field and check the reference against that commit, not the working tree.

rules.statement: Don't report as a breaking change a minor-release change that gives a documented exception to input that never worked, such as a length above int.MaxValue that previously failed with an undocumented exception.
rules.why: Code written against the documentation sees no change, so documenting a new exception for input that could never succeed is acceptable in a minor release when the changelog records it.
rules.check: Before flagging an exception-type change as semver-major, check whether the old exception was documented and whether the input could ever succeed before; confirm the changelog's Changed entry records it.

rules.statement: Don't report new entries added directly to PublicAPI.Shipped.txt when the pull request is the release commit for that version.
rules.why: The release change moves the unshipped entries into PublicAPI.Shipped.txt and leaves PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt holding only `#nullable enable`.
rules.check: Before flagging Shipped additions, check whether the version file and CHANGELOG show this PR releases the version and whether PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt is left empty except `#nullable enable`.

rules.statement: Don't ask to replace a public enum with an open strategy when every member names something the library implements itself and callers can't plug in new members, and don't ask for a throwing default switch arm that earlier validation makes unreachable.
rules.why: An enum is kept for members fixed by the code itself, so adding one is an additive change; a default arm that no test can reach is dead code to delete.
rules.check: Check whether callers can extend the set, and whether a validation step rejects undefined enum values before the switch runs.

rules.statement: A member documented to throw ObjectDisposedException after Dispose must check disposal before any shortcut, such as a ReferenceEquals check in Equals, that could return early.
rules.why: Otherwise a disposed instance compared with itself returns true instead of the documented exception, hiding use-after-dispose.
rules.check: Look at Equals and similar methods on disposable types for a same-instance or other fast path that runs before the disposal check.

rules.statement: Documentation on which members throw after Dispose must match the code and name the members, such as Flush, FlushAsync or canceled-token paths, that don't throw.
rules.why: A caller who relies on the docs would expect a throw that never comes.
rules.check: Compare class remarks claiming 'every member throws after Dispose' against members that skip the disposal check.

rules.statement: In a test project, test a helper that rents a buffer and disposes it when filling fails by checking that the rental was returned and zeroed, not only that the exception was thrown.
rules.why: If the test only checks the exception type, deleting the dispose from the catch block leaves the suite green, and secret data could stay in an unzeroed pooled buffer.
rules.check: Look for failure-path tests on rent-and-fill helpers that assert only the exception type; each Span and Memory overload needs coverage.

rules.statement: In a test project, assert metric meter names, instrument units and tag keys and values as string literals, not through the library's internal constants.
rules.why: Dashboards depend on these names, and a test that reads the constants won't catch a rename.
rules.check: Look for metrics tests that compare against internal constants, or that skip the unit on some counters.

rules.statement: When several types implement the same sizing or growth rule and constant, move them into one internal helper that all of them call.
rules.why: If the rule changes in one type, the copies in the other types can keep the old rule.
rules.check: Look for duplicated required/doubled/minimum capacity computations and repeated minimum-size constants across buffer types.

rules.statement: Implement a Span overload by calling its Memory sibling and returning memory.Span, rather than repeating the validation, sizing, rental and dispose-on-throw body in each overload.
rules.why: If each overload repeats the body, a fix to failure handling or sizing in one can miss its sibling.
rules.check: Look for Span/Memory overload pairs whose bodies duplicate the rent-and-fill logic.

rules.statement: When a method returns a pooled owner together with an out Span or Memory view, its XML docs must say that the view is valid only until the returned owner is disposed.
rules.why: A caller could keep using the view after disposing the owner and read zeros or another renter's data.
rules.check: Check the <param> or <returns> docs of rent helpers with out Span/Memory parameters for a statement about how long the view is valid.

rules.statement: Give new private and internal helpers a /// summary, plus <returns> when the return value carries a contract, such as a count of elements written or an owner that the caller must dispose.
rules.why: Otherwise maintainers have to read method bodies to learn these contracts.
rules.check: Look for new non-public methods and properties without /// docs, especially ones whose return value must be disposed or is a count.

rules.statement: Document an internal member that exists only for tests as test-only.
rules.why: Otherwise a later refactor can't tell that the member exists only to give tests access.
rules.check: Look for internal members whose only readers are in test projects and whose docs don't say so.

rules.statement: Wrap edited Markdown/MDX prose paragraphs evenly at about 120 columns, and write identifiers such as meter names and constants as code spans.
rules.why: This keeps edits consistent with the rest of the docs, and a wrap check may flag long lines.
rules.check: Look in edited doc paragraphs for lines well past 120 columns, uneven wraps, or identifiers in plain text.

rules.statement: When citing an ADR from another project, such as the project template, include that project's prefix (for example 'project-template ADR-0113').
rules.why: Without the prefix, readers may take it for one of this project's own records.
rules.check: Look in ADRs and docs for ADR numbers outside this project's own numbering range that have no project prefix.

rules.statement: In a test project, tests of argument validation must assert the exception's ParamName, not just use a bare Assert.Throws.
rules.why: Without ParamName, the test still passes if a different check, or one on the wrong parameter, rejects the input.
rules.check: Look for Assert.Throws<ArgumentException/ArgumentNullException/ArgumentOutOfRangeException> whose result's ParamName isn't checked.

rules.statement: In a test project, don't check many members or cases in one test; split them into one fact per behavior or a [Theory] over the cases.
rules.why: The first failing assertion hides the rest, and the test name doesn't say which member broke.
rules.check: Look for single tests asserting many members (for example after Dispose) or many unrelated argument cases.
